target_customer: Robotics and physical AI labs that buy training data with force and contact labels
problem: Video-only robot training data carries no force or touch information. Hemlock records worker hand activity with EMG wearables to add force and contact labels.
business_model: Data foundry selling annotated egocentric datasets to physical AI developers
product_category: Physical AI training data and EMG wearable hardware

founders.name: Julian Olschwang
education: Left the Electrical and Computer Engineering program at Carnegie Mellon University without finishing
founders.background_notes: YC page says he holds four wearable technology patents and built GANs for robotic data generation at UCLA.

competitors.name: Unidata
competitors.what: Multimodal egocentric capture system for humanoid training datasets

competitors.name: Human Archive
competitors.what: Egocentric robot training data collected from gig workers
competitors.funding_then: Seed reported in May 2026; sources conflict between $8.2M and $82M

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs custom EMG hardware, signal processing and synchronization with video, plus a method to turn muscle signals into force labels. A solo founder with wearable patents did this.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary Bracelet hardware and a force-labelled dataset are harder to copy than plain video, but the egocentric data market was crowded by mid 2026.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Unknown; company is newly in the Fall 2026 batch. Incumbent names are unsourced context.

market_need_then: Robotics labs were buying large volumes of human video in 2026, and one source cites Skild noting that video lacks force and torque. Hemlock claims adding its data raised egg pick-and-place success tenfold on Pi0.5, a company claim reported by Fondo.

identity.visual_style: Dark minimal with glowing cyan muscle-signal effects and a black Bracelet

brand_strength.rationale: Early; a Fondo feature exists but no community signals. Hemlock is also a poison and a CMU text editor name, which search results showed dominating the name.

outcome_analysis: Hemlock is an active one-person Fall 2026 YC company selling force-labelled egocentric data for robots, so no outcome exists yet. The idea rides a real data scarcity in physical AI, but a solo founder, crowded data vendors and the need to prove buyers pay for force labels are the open questions.
notes: Funding unverified: Dealroom lists a $500k seed without date or investors, single aggregator, so not recorded as a round. No funding press found. Outcome search returned unrelated pages (Hemlock text editor), no shutdown or acquisition found. Founder details come from the YC page only.
